questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: explain the role of a masking agent
questions.stem: In the replicate spectrophotometric assay exercise below, a instructor reports these measurements. In an EDTA titration of calcium in the presence of magnesium, a masking agent is added. What is its role?

options.text: It makes EDTA react faster with every metal in solution
options.misconception: confuses masking with a general rate catalyst

options.text: It increases the indicator color intensity without affecting metal ions
options.misconception: mistakes a mask for a color enhancer

options.text: It lowers the pH so that all complexes become unstable
options.misconception: mistakes masking for pH adjustment

options.text: It binds the interfering magnesium selectively so EDTA reacts only with the analyte

questions.explanation: A masking agent forms a stable complex with an interfering ion, removing it from competition for EDTA without changing the analyte. It is selective toward the interferent rather than a universal accelerator or a pH control.
questions.hint: Masking hides an interferent selectively.

questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: explain metallochromic indicator selection
questions.stem: In the replicate spectrophotometric assay exercise below, a instructor notes the observed value. Why must a metallochromic indicator used in an EDTA titration form a metal complex weaker than the metal EDTA complex?

options.text: So the indicator complex is strong enough to hold the metal forever
options.misconception: reverses the required relative stability

options.text: So the indicator itself is not colored before complexation
options.misconception: confuses relative stability with the color of the free form

options.text: So EDTA can displace the metal from the indicator at the endpoint, producing a sharp color change
So the indicator can be added in large excess without error
options.misconception: mistakes stability for an allowance on indicator amount

questions.explanation: The indicator must bind the metal weakly enough that EDTA, with the larger formation constant, strips the metal away at the endpoint. If the indicator complex were stronger, the color would never change and no endpoint could be detected.
questions.hint: The titrant must win the metal away from the indicator.

options.text: It makes EDTA react faster with every metal in solution
options.misconception: confuses masking with a general rate catalyst

options.text: It increases the indicator color intensity without affecting metal ions
options.misconception: mistakes a mask for a color enhancer

options.text: It lowers the pH so that all complexes become unstable
options.misconception: mistakes masking for pH adjustment

options.text: It binds the interfering magnesium selectively so EDTA reacts only with the analyte

questions.explanation: A masking agent forms a stable complex with an interfering ion, removing it from competition for EDTA without changing the analyte. It is selective toward the interferent rather than a universal accelerator or a pH control.
questions.hint: Masking hides an interferent selectively.

options.text: So the indicator complex is strong enough to hold the metal forever
options.misconception: reverses the required relative stability

options.text: So the indicator itself is not colored before complexation
